items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: King Oliver was sitting for him to come to Chicago, Joe Oliver.

ctx.x: mother's side. Yeah. Mm-hmm. Anyway, I have a lot more to ask you. Were there any saloons in your neighborhood? You said you played at different places, but would you play at places in your neighborhood?

No, no. There were saloons in the neighborhood, but they didn't have any music. Now, there was music downtown, and some of the places uptown, like the Pigpen. Did you go to the Pigpen? Oh, I went there once. Now those are the players who played, like the Pigpen and some of those old places, Louis Armstrong played there. See, a lot of people think that Louis Armstrong played on Bourbon Street. Because people come in and ask me, they say, oh, did Louis Armstrong play here? No. And when he played at Preservation…
with Fletcher Henderson. Well, you mentioned the Pigpen. Did you ever, that was on Decatur Street?
